I don't think a lot of people realize what's going on (what's been going on). I've worked with journalists and bloggers so I have a unique perspective on this as a whole. The reporting industry has been in flux due to the blogging expansion on the internet. Mainstream reporting outlets have had to compete with smaller blogging outlets for advertising dollars and their budgets (which were previously bloated like a pregnant whale) have caused major deficits and near bankruptcies. Combine this with the economy shrinking and advertising companies re-evaluating where they put their customers' advertising money. The advert bubble is starting to burst. Since the advertising dollars are shrinking, the news and reporting budgets are starting to as well. This has all been happening over the last 12-24 months or so.

Now throw in GamerGate. We've already seen reorganizations and layoffs of games sites and journalists. There will be more. GamerGate is not totally responsible. But GG has hurt these people. Badly. My point is this: Advertisers do not like controversy. They like happy customers. Gaming sites cannot afford to be hit with letter writing campaigns at this point in time. At about the same time that Hatman declared rule revisions, Acidman had his own "purge" of shitposters. The problem was that unlike Reddit, the banned posters were at the time still anonymous to the community, resulting in verification to be placed on the belief that the mod team was acting in good faith. A few clever shitposters that were going to get the axe used this window to criticize the mods, thus making it look like the mods were banning for disagreement with the policy. Boycott discussions had not been allowed for some time, so a steady some of users formed a new board, /ggrevolt/, comprising of those skeptical of Acid and from shitposters banned from hq. The resulting in-board fighting limited content output for the rest of GamerGate as the community became fractured, discussion was focused on the drama, and the division has still not fully healed thanks to the number of unique IPs decreasing from the drama.

Shortly afterwards, FPH was banned, causing KiA to skyrocket in popularity.
